newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar up on festival buying, new supplies.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar up on festival buying, new supplies.

text.p: Sugar prices looked up on the local market on Thursday, dealers said.
"Fresh physical buying ahead of Diwali dragged prices upward, while supplies remained at low ebb," a dealer said.
Most delivery tenders from the mills out of the quota for October are exhausted, they said. This in turn curtailed arrivals from mills to the market.

"Actually government has increased supplies of sugar to public distribution system but quality of sugar remained inferior," one broker said. "Now consumer is turning to open market for superior variety for festival buying."

In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 3/12 rupees to 1,315/1,350 rupees per quintal while M-30 moved up by 10/15 rupees to 1,350/1,380 rupees per quintal. Sugar mill delivery for 1st November was quoted at 1,240/1,250 rupees per quintal.
